stem: What is the most common initial troubleshooting step used to resolve general mobile OS and application issues?
explanation: Power cycling (restarting) the device is the least invasive first step.

stem: A user reports that a mobile app fails to launch on their smartphone. Which of the options listed below is the best initial troubleshooting step to resolve this issue?
explanation: Start with the least invasive fix: restart the device. Clearing the cache or data comes later.

stem: To force stop a mobile app means to: (Select all that apply)
explanation: A force stop ends all of the app's processes in both the foreground and the background. It doesn't disable the app or revoke permissions.
options: Terminate all processes related to the app
Stop the app from running in the foreground
Disable the app until it is manually re-enabled
Revoke permissions granted to the app
Stop the app from running in the background
correctAnswer: Terminate all processes related to the app
Stop the app from running in the foreground
Stop the app from running in the background

stem: For each mobile app troubleshooting action on the left select the root cause it is primarily intended to resolve (according to the standard least-invasive-first methodology).
explanation: Each action targets a specific cause: reinstall fixes corrupted app files, clearing cache/data fixes corrupted temporary or user data, an update fixes known bugs, a restart clears memory conflicts and hung processes, and a force close stops a frozen app.
options: Core application files are corrupted, incomplete, mismatched, or fail integrity checks
Crashes or misbehavior are caused by corrupted temporary files, cached data, or user-specific settings
Known bugs or compatibility issues have been fixed in a newer version of the app
Crashes are caused by temporary memory conflicts, hung processes, or system resource issues
An app is unresponsive, frozen, or stuck in a loop

correctAnswer.Reinstall the app: Core application files are corrupted, incomplete, mismatched, or fail integrity checks
correctAnswer.Clear the app cache/data: Crashes or misbehavior are caused by corrupted temporary files, cached data, or user-specific settings
correctAnswer.Update the app: Known bugs or compatibility issues have been fixed in a newer version of the app
correctAnswer.Restart the device: Crashes are caused by temporary memory conflicts, hung processes, or system resource issues
correctAnswer.Force close the app: An app is unresponsive, frozen, or stuck in a loop

stem: A mobile device cannot update an app, and the system displays an error related to account authentication. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: An authentication error points to expired app store credentials.
options: App store access restricted by firewall

stem: A user reports that a mobile app from the official app store will not install on a company-managed smartphone. What is the most likely reason for this issue?
explanation: On a company-managed device, MDM policy restrictions commonly block installs.

stem: Which of the following actions would be of help while troubleshooting a mobile app that becomes slow to respond?
explanation: All of these can improve a slow-responding app.
options: Force stop and relaunch the app

stem: Most mobile OS updates require a minimum battery percentage or a charging status to prevent the device from shutting down during the update process.
explanation: True. Updates require enough battery or a charger.

stem: An OS update installation begins on a mobile device but consistently stops and reverses the process at 75% complete. The device has plenty of free space and is on a fast network. What does this behavior most strongly suggest?
explanation: With enough space and a fast network, an update that rolls back partway suggests a corrupted update package.

stem: A user is troubleshooting a personally-owned mobile device that repeatedly fails to initiate an operating system update. The device is currently connected to a known good home office Wi-Fi network, plugged into a charger, and the update package is confirmed to be available for download. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the update failure?
explanation: Network and power are fine and the device is personal (no MDM), so insufficient free storage space is the most likely cause.

stem: A tablet's battery drains unusually fast even when the device is idle. Which of the actions listed below will most likely resolve the issue?
explanation: Idle battery drain usually comes from background apps, so identify and restrict them.
options: Reduce the screen brightness to its minimum
Check for physical damage to the battery

stem: A mobile device repeatedly loses battery charge in areas with no reliable cellular coverage. Which action can most effectively reduce the battery drain?
explanation: The radio keeps searching for a signal, so airplane mode stops the drain.

stem: A corrupted OS installation has been isolated as the most likely cause of persistent random reboots on a user's mobile device. After backing up all user data and charging the device, what is the next troubleshooting step a technician should take?
explanation: With a corrupted OS and the data backed up, the fix is a factory reset.
options: Check for and install the latest OS update
Downgrade the OS to the previous stable version
Perform a factory reset of the device
correctAnswer: Perform a factory reset of the device

stem: A technician observes that a mobile device reboots randomly during high CPU/GPU load. Which of the following is the most probable cause?
explanation: High CPU/GPU load generates heat, and overheating causes random reboots.

stem: Bluetooth connectivity issues on a mobile device can be resolved by: (Select all that apply)
explanation: Bluetooth fixes include keeping the devices close, toggling Bluetooth, restarting both devices and re-pairing. An access point is irrelevant to Bluetooth.
options: Moving the device closer to an access point
Ensuring the connecting devices are adequately close to each other
Turning Bluetooth off and then turning it on again
Unpairing and then re-pairing the device
correctAnswer: Ensuring the connecting devices are adequately close to each other
Turning Bluetooth off and then turning it on again
Unpairing and then re-pairing the device

stem: Which of the actions listed below will have no effect on resolving Wi-Fi connectivity issues on a mobile device?
explanation: The SIM card is used for cellular service and has no effect on Wi-Fi.
options: Move the device closer to the wireless router
Reseat the mobile device's SIM card
Verify the correctness of Wi-Fi credentials
correctAnswer: Reseat the mobile device's SIM card

stem: Which of the following is not a valid troubleshooting step for resolving problems with contactless payment transactions on a mobile device?
explanation: Airplane mode turns off NFC, so it would break contactless payments rather than fix them.
options: Ensure the phone is awake and unlocked
If used, remove the device's EMF/RFID protective case
Verify payment card details in the mobile wallet app
Maintain very close proximity between the phone and the terminal
Enable airplane mode to reduce wireless interference
correctAnswer: Enable airplane mode to reduce wireless interference

stem: Modern mobile devices have the capability to automatically present landscape or portrait views of the device's screen based on how the device is being held. If the screen does not auto-rotate, the easiest troubleshooting step is to modify the appropriate system settings, such as disabling Portrait Orientation Lock on Apple devices or enabling Auto-rotate on Android devices.
explanation: True. Check the orientation lock or auto-rotate setting first.

stem: What is the name of the package file format used by the Android OS for the distribution and installation of mobile applications?
explanation: APK is the Android package format. IPA is for iOS.

stem: The practice of installing mobile apps from untrusted sources (i.e., websites and app stores other than the official marketplaces) is referred to as:
explanation: Sideloading is installing apps from outside the official store.

stem: Sideloading via APK is the primary method for installing unverified apps from third-party sites on:
explanation: APK sideloading is an Android method.

stem: Installing mobile apps from the official, trusted sources such as Apple's App Store or Google Play significantly reduces malware-related security risks.
explanation: True. Official stores vet the apps they distribute.

stem: What is the name of an iOS/Android feature that provides access to advanced system settings hidden by default from regular users?
explanation: Developer Mode (developer options) exposes advanced settings hidden by default.

stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to the process of granting a regular user elevated privileges on an Android-based mobile device?
explanation: Rooting gives a user root (superuser) access on Android.

stem: The process of bypassing Apple's built-in software restrictions on iOS/iPadOS devices is known as:
explanation: Jailbreaking removes Apple's software restrictions on iOS/iPadOS.

stem: Which of the following enables installation of software that is not available through the official Apple App Store?
explanation: Jailbreaking lets an Apple device install software outside the App Store.

stem: Which of the answers listed below best describes the concept of application spoofing?
explanation: Application spoofing is a malicious app that disguises itself as a legitimate one.
options: A situation in which a web form field accepts data other than expected (e.g., server commands)
A type of attack aimed at exploiting an unknown vulnerability in already released software
A mobile app performing unwanted and harmful actions in disguise of a legitimate and useful program
A method for gaining unauthorized root access to a mobile device's operating system
correctAnswer: A mobile app performing unwanted and harmful actions in disguise of a legitimate and useful program

stem: Which of the following actions would be the best initial diagnostic step to identify the source of excessive traffic on a mobile device?
explanation: Per-app data usage logs show which app is generating the traffic.

stem: Which of the actions listed below would most likely improve degraded response times on a mobile device? (Select 3 answers)
explanation: Updates, closing background apps and restarting improve responsiveness. The quiz marked reviewing resource usage and developer options as not correct.
options: Installing operating system or application updates
Reviewing CPU, RAM, or storage usage for resource-heavy apps
Enabling developer options to generate more detailed system logs
Restarting the device to clear temporary processes
correctAnswer: Installing operating system or application updates
Restarting the device to clear temporary processes

stem: A mobile device repeatedly displays data-usage limit notifications despite minimal user activity. Which condition is most likely the direct cause of this symptom?
explanation: Unexpected high data use points to a malicious app.

stem: A user reports their mobile device frequently loses Wi-Fi connection or cannot connect to any networks. Which of the following would be the most targeted and least disruptive troubleshooting step to resolve this problem?
explanation: Restarting the Wi-Fi adapter targets the problem directly with the least disruption.
options: Remove and reinsert the device's SIM card
Perform a hard reboot (forced restart) of the device
Forget all networks from the device's saved Wi-Fi list and try to reconnect
Restart the device's Wi-Fi adapter to reset the connection
correctAnswer: Restart the device's Wi-Fi adapter to reset the connection

stem: If a mobile device intermittently loses Wi-Fi connection, which action will have no effect on improving its stability?
explanation: The SIM card handles cellular service and doesn't affect Wi-Fi stability.
options: Forget and reconnect to the Wi-Fi network
Move closer to the Wi-Fi router or access point
Restart the Wi-Fi adapter on the device
Check for and reduce Wi-Fi interference from other devices
Remove and reinsert the device's SIM card
correctAnswer: Remove and reinsert the device's SIM card

stem: A technician is troubleshooting a mobile device with no internet connectivity. They notice the device is also experiencing rapid battery drain and high data usage alerts. After isolating the device from the network, what should the technician do next?
explanation: The symptoms suggest malware, so scan for it after isolating the device.

stem: After installing an application from outside the Google Play Store, an Android user notices that the device is displaying an excessive number of advertisements, including pop-ups appearing outside of the web browser. What is the most likely explanation for this issue?
explanation: Apps from outside the official store can contain adware, which shows excessive ads.

stem: The primary goal of delivering a fake security warning to a mobile device user is to:
explanation: Fake security warnings aim to trick the user into installing malicious software.
options: Mislead the user into disabling real security features
Trick the user into installing malicious software
Misinform the user about the device's actual security status
Pressure the user into buying a legitimate third-party app
correctAnswer: Trick the user into installing malicious software

stem: An Android user reports that several system settings change back to default automatically and the device frequently reboots. A technician discovers Developer Mode was enabled and an application was sideloaded from a third-party website. What is the most effective method to completely remove the threat and restore the device to normal operation?
explanation: A factory reset removes the threat completely and restores normal operation.
options: Perform a factory reset of the device
correctAnswer: Perform a factory reset of the device

stem: An employee notices their private photos and contacts have been posted to a public social media site without their consent. A technician inspects the device and finds apps with administrative privileges that the user does not remember installing. What is the best course of action to fully remediate the device and remove unauthorized access?
explanation: Apps with administrative privileges that the user never installed mean the device is compromised, so reset it to factory defaults.
options: Reset the device to factory defaults
correctAnswer: Reset the device to factory defaults
